subject: Seasonal uptime exception and monthly credit structure — Evercrest negotiation
messages:
From: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@evercrest.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@evercrest.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Seasonal SLA exception request and credit mechanics

Sergio —

Thanks for taking this. We’re finalizing our vendor SLA template and want to put Redwood’s standard uptime/credit language on the table so our procurement and finance teams can evaluate. A few specifics from our side:

- Baseline uptime target we expect: 99.95% (annualized) — can you confirm Redwood’s standard?
- We run heavy month-end batch inference for three business days each month (approx. 72 hours) where traffic spikes 4–6x; we need a proposal for a seasonal/operational exception window and how credits would apply.
- Credit cap: finance prefers an explicit monthly cap rather than open-ended credits.
- Latency: our product needs p95 inference under 300ms for synchronous calls — would like a latency SLO (and related remedies) in the SLA.

Can you share a revised SLA template that shows: baseline uptime, how a month-end exception is carved out (duration/limits), a sample monthly-credit calculation, and a proposal for a credit cap? Claire (copied) and I will route to legal once we have something concrete.

Best,
Claire Hughes
VP, Infrastructure & ML
Evercrest AI
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@evercrest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 14:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA exception request and credit mechanics

Claire — thanks for the clear ask. Attaching an initial draft of an SLA tailored to the month-end pattern you described (SLA_Proposal_Evercrest_v1.pdf). High level proposal below so you can share internally quickly: 

- Baseline uptime: 99.90% (monthly measurement). Redwood’s standard hosted SLA is 99.90% with a tiered remedy schedule; we can discuss bumping to 99.95% with a small commercial uplift.
- Seasonal exception: we can provide a month-end operational exception window of up to 72 hours per calendar month during which availability guarantees are relaxed to 99.50% for services which are batch-optimized. Exceptions must be scheduled (or predictable recurring window) or triggered by documented capacity anomalies.
- Monthly credits: Credits calculated as percentage of the monthly Redwood service fees, prorated by minutes below the SLA threshold. Example bands in the attached: 99.90–99.75 => 5% of monthly invoice, 99.75–99.50 => 15%, <99.50 => 30% (subject to cap).
- Credit cap: propose 20% of monthly invoice as a conservative commercial cap. This keeps exposure bounded while providing material remediation.
- Latency: we usually avoid hard latency-based credits for multi-tenant hosted models, but can add a p95 target of 300ms with a non-monetary remediation (first-fix SLA/priority routing) and a lower monetary remedy band if clear production regressions are observed.

Next steps: Laura (legal) — can you review the credit band language and cap? Marissa (CS) — help me confirm operational constraints for the batch-optimized services referenced. Claire — if this is close, we can do a quick 30-min alignment call and proceed to redlines.

Attachments: SLA_Proposal_Evercrest_v1.pdf (summary + example credit calc)

Cheers,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 09:18:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA exception request and credit mechanics

Quick legal take after an initial pass on the attached draft:

- Credit mechanics: prefer discrete tiers with a clear proration formula. Suggest replacing the open 'prorated by minutes' language with a minutes-based formula in the attachment (we’ve included a redline PDF: SLA_Redlines_Legal_20270119.pdf).
- Cap: 20% cap is acceptable commercial starting point; propose an escrow/recoupment carve where credits above 15% require documented post-mortem and remediation plan. This protects Redwood from recurring failures.
- Seasonal exception: tighten the definition so an exception is either pre-scheduled (e.g., 72h recurring window with notice) or requires customer-provided evidence of legitimate traffic spike. Exceptions shouldn’t be self-declared post-fact.
- Latency SLO: recommend making latency a monitoring/operational SLO with a remediation play (priority routing, dedicated burst) rather than a credit-triggering financial SLO — but if Evercrest insists, we can introduce a narrow monetary band (small % of fees) for p95 > 300ms sustained over a rolling 24h.

I’ve attached the redlines. If Evercrest accepts the 20% cap and the escrow condition above, legal can prepare a version for signature.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference
From: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@evercrest.ai>
To: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@evercrest.ai, rmendez@evercrest.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA exception request and credit mechanics

Sergio / Laura — thanks for the draft and the redlines. A few counterpoints from procurement/engineering after reviewing: 

- Baseline uptime: Evercrest’s procurement team is pushing for 99.95% baseline. We’re willing to accept a modest uplift on fees, but 99.90 will materially complicate our procurement approval.
- Credit cap: we prefer an explicit monthly cap but would ask the cap be 25% rather than 20% given the business criticality of the inference pipeline.
- Seasonal exception: we absolutely need the 72-hour month-end window for batch loads; however, Evercrest requests that credits still accrue for service impact outside scheduled maintenance or excluded runs. If an exception is pre-scheduled and used to run batch jobs, we accept a reduced remedy but not full carve-out.
- Latency: we can accept a non-monetary remediation for latency as a first step, but ask that the SLA include a path to monetary remedy if p95 > 300ms for more than 48 continuous hours.

I’ve uploaded our counter-SLA with a few inline comments (Evercrest_SLA_Countersign_v1.pdf). If Redwood can accept: baseline 99.95, cap 25%, and a combined approach to the seasonal exception (scheduled window with reduced remedy but not full exclusion), we can move quickly.

Regards,
Claire
VP, Infrastructure & ML
Evercrest AI
From: sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Claire Hughes <claire.hughes@evercrest.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 16:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Seasonal SLA exception request and credit mechanics

Claire — appreciate the thoughtful counter. Proposing a compromise to unblock procurement while keeping commercial risk bounded: 

- Baseline uptime: agree to 99.92% baseline for the pilot year (midpoint). If you require 99.95% as a hard commitment, we can do that with a 7.5% commercial uplift to fees — happy to model both.
- Credit cap: accept 22.5% cap as a middle ground (we can round in the final doc to 22%). Credits above 15% require written post-mortem and remediation plan (Laura’s escrow carve).
- Seasonal exception: schedule up to 72h / month-end window. During that scheduled window the availability threshold for batch-optimized endpoints will be 99.5% and remedies reduced by 50% (credits still apply but at a lower band). For unscheduled impacts during heavy runs, full remedies apply.
- Latency: include p95 300ms as an operational SLO. If p95 > 300ms for 48 continuous hours, trigger an elevated remediation ladder: priority routing + a monetary band (2% monthly fee per sustained 24h over threshold, capped by the overall credit cap).

Next steps: Laura — can you incorporate the 22% cap and the 50% reduction in seasonal-window remedies into the redline PDF and push to DocuSign? Claire — if that looks good, can we schedule a 30-min call Thurs or Fri to finalize? I’ll attach a summary and include the DocuSign draft link.

Attachments: SLA_Redlines_Legal_20270119.pdf; DocuSign: https://docusign.com/EVERCREST-SLA-20270119

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
